pr_title: refactor(compiler): support interpolation and encoded entities when lexing markup
pr_body:
The lexer now splits interpolation and encoded entity tokens out from the string it is tokenizing.

See individual commits...

Fixes #41034
pr_comments: Quick update after running a subset of targets in g3 (blueprint presubmit): there are few broken targets, related to the changes in this PR. I'll investigate more and try to extract specific cases (in a form of a minimal repro), so that we can also extend our test coverage.

FYI I've started [a new presubmit](http://test/OCL:379395451:BASE:379579995:1623793954177:de316e82) with the most recent changes from this PR, since there were some changes that would help resolve issues in the failing targets (thanks @JoostK for bringing it up!). Will keep this thread updated.

Another update after running a new presubmit: it looks like the previous problem went away. There are few broken targets currently caused by unterminated interpolation expressions in a template (note the missing `}}`):
```
<my-comp title="{{ a ? 'a' : 'b' "> ... </my-comp>
```

The error message is:

```
error TS-995002: Opening tag "my-comp" not terminated.
```

I will update templates as needed, but wanted to share this in case there is an easy way to detect this situation and throw an error about unterminated interpolation vs not terminated tag (and to check whether this makes sense or the current error is better).
Thanks @AndrewKushnir, I think I can make the error message better in these cases.

One more case that I was able to extract from the broken targets: ```
<ng-template let-suggestion> {{suggestion}} </ng-template>
``` the error message is: ``` error TS-995002: Unexpected closing tag "section". It may happen when the tag has already been closed by another tag. For more info see https://www.w3.org/TR/html5/syntax.html#closing-elements-that-have-implied-end-tags 8 ~~~~~~~~~~ ``` It looks like everything after `{{` is considered a content of an interpolation (which might be correct?). A couple additional things I tried: - removing the inner `
` avoids the problem (which is a bit surprising) - adding `ngNonBindable` to the `` element doesn't help (seems to have no effect), which might be something we'd need to investigate @petebacondarwin please let me know if you're able to repro this locally as well (just tested that in g3, not locally).

Actually, it seems that the current template parser thinks that this is valid. See https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-ivy-nkqqjy?file=src%2Fapp%2Fapp.component.html

And moreover, it looks like people are using it as a way to escape interpolation in their templates.

So we should not error in this case.
@AndrewKushnir - I think I have removed and potential new error reports, to ensure backward compatibility. Would you be able to start a new presubmit perhaps?

New presubmit indicated a different breakage now. Here is a minimal repro: ``` 
import {A} from 'a';
``` The error message: ``` error TS-995002: Unexpected character "EOF" (Do you have an unescaped "{" in your template? Use "{{ '{' }}") to escape it.) ``` While the error makes sense, it seems like it used to work before.
I have found that this is actually a bug in the original lexer and created a pre-emptive fix for it, which we should land before this PR: https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/42605
I've rebased this on top of #42605 so that we can get some feedback from CI. Once that other PR lands, I will rebase again and then ask for more reviews.
[Presubmit](http://test/OCL:384250765:BASE:384250948:1626107178061:c834ba50) (note: we'll also need to start a global one).
[Global Presubmit](https://test.corp.google.com/OCL:385334299:BASE:385334350:1626546947811:b4b394fb).
[Global Presubmit #2](https://test.corp.google.com/OCL:386157821:BASE:386157840:1626927475889:9a0fc7b0).
[Global Presubmit #3](https://test.corp.google.com/OCL:388142618:BASE:388142664:1627878964854:98434b4e).

FYI, global presubmit is successful, this PR should be ready for merge!

Confirmed with Pete that it's on to add the "merge" label.

FYI, reopening this PR since it was rolled back due to the issues in g3. Specifically, extracted message (xi18n) that contained `&ngsp;`, `&` (and potentially other HTML entities) had a different message id, triggering re-translations. Unfortunately, these problems were not caught by the global presubmit (TGP). We would need to make sure that:

- we have extra test coverage for xi18n for messages with HTML entities
- there are extra presubmits internally that verify that no message ids were changed unexpectedly

Also before landing the change again, we'd need to run i18n extraction for the affected app.

@petebacondarwin could you please have a look at the i18n extraction once you're back?

Previously if there are interpolations in a message then you end up with an i18n “container” node, which is serialized to something like:

```
[text, ${ph}, text] 
```

After this PR, encoded entities are sort of treated like interpolations so we ended up getting:

```
'[before , &,  after]'
```

rather than

```
'before & after`
```

The digest value that is then generated from these strings is obviously different.

# 🐞 Bug report ### Command (mark with an `x`) - [ ] new - [ ] build - [ ] serve - [ ] test - [ ] e2e - [ ] generate - [ ] add - [ ] update - [ ] lint - [x] extract-i18n - [ ] run - [ ] config - [ ] help - [ ] version - [ ] doc ### Is this a regression? Yes, I also tested this with the old extraction tool (`"@angular/cli": "~9.1.15"`) and it works correctly with `ng xi18n`. ### Description Placing an [HTML entity](https://dev.w3.org/html5/html-author/charref) (e.g. ` `) inside a translated text which also contains interpolated variables (`
 Interpolation: {{ variable }}
`) results in an incorrect value of the `equiv-text` attribute inside the extracted message's `INTERPOLATION` tag (``). Seems like the value is shifted by the difference in amount of characters taken up by the HTML entity and it's actual representation. This is a minor and rather unimportant issue since it does not affect the actual interpolation or translation. From what I understand this `equiv-text` attribute has an informative role for translators. ## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction [https://github.com/pKrupaJunior/extract-i18n-issue](https://github.com/pKrupaJunior/extract-i18n-issue) 1. Create project: ```shell ng new extract-i18n-issue -s -t --minimal -g -S --style css --create-application false ``` 2. Create sample application: ```shell ng g application demo -s -t --minimal --style css -S --routing false ``` 3. Add localization support: ```shell ng add @angular/localize ``` 4. Add an HTML template containing `i18n` attribute on a tag with **interpolated variables** and **HTML entities**: ```html
Interpolation: {{ one }} Interpolation: {{ two }}
``` 5. Run `extract-i18n`: ```shell ng extract-i18n --output-path projects/demo/src/i18n ``` ## 🔥 Result The generated `messages.xlf` file contains this: ```xml Interpolation:  Interpolation: ... ``` The second `equiv-text` attribute value is incorrect: ``. While it should be: ``. ## 🌍 Your Environment 
Angular CLI: 11.1.4
Node: 12.13.0
OS: win32 x64

comments:
So the problem is that our lexer decodes such entities into their actual characters but the whole decoded text block is passed to the parser that then splits out the interpolation blocks. The parser then works with the characters in the text blocks, which have lost the original positions of the encoded characters...

For example the tokens lexed fron the example given include:

```
TAG_OPEN_START: 'div'
ATTR_NAME: 'i18n'
TAG_OPEN_END: 'div'
TEXT: 'Interpolation: {{ one }} Interpolation: {{ two }}'
TAG_CLOSE: 'div'
```

Notice that the TEXT token holds both interpolations but the ` ` sequence has been decoded into a single NBSP character.
The only real solution is to actually capture these interpolations as tokens in their own right with their own source-spans, and then change the parsers to handle this.

review_comments: In `_consumeText`, these parts used to be joined and go through `_processCarriageReturns`; especially omitting the latter may cause different behavior?
I think that carriage returns in interpolation expressions are not so common, but I will add that processing to the individual parts.
We don't want to join these but I have added in the CR processing for each part..
This seems like a spurious change - should it be included here?

Very spurious! Not sure how that ended up in this PR!

Since this `Task` is not used in the file, it is a valid clean up. I'll move it to its own commit in this PR, since it would be a bit overkill to create a whole PR just for this.

I got a bit confused here because this appears to leave the `this._beginToken(TokenType.ENCODED_ENTITY);` at the method's start unclosed, but looking at it more closely that doesn't matter. Maybe it would be clearer to only begin the `ENCODED_ENTITY` token if we are sure it is parsed as such.

That would require calling beginToken in multiple places for the main use cases of this function.
I feel that since this is an alternative use case, it is better to make this the exception. I'll add a comment to make this more clear.

Was that a test with the current compiler, or after this PR?

Are you suggesting that we leave this comment here because something should change in this PR? Or just as a reminder that we might want to revisit this in a future PR?
I wish the token parts would be documented better, this is a bit magical. Perhaps a const enum would help clarify these indices.
I am going to add discriminated interfaces for each token type in a separate commit.
This has been done in the "refactor(compiler): define interfaces for each lexer token" commit.
